title: Interpriting
body:
Translation and execution is done at the same time
Both Interpreting and [[Compiling]] languages are converted to [[Machine Language]] 
Python is an Interpreted language. 

***Downsides of interpretation***
Using Python as an example, 
Your source code must be on the computer every time you execute it.

[[Python]] and [[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTER SCIENCE]] are the other end of this: that course is
taught in the interpreted language, this one in the compiled one, and most of the differences
between them come back to the line above. The second consequence worth adding: with no compile
step there is no compile-time type check either, so [[Errors]] shift one column right.
